content:
Rumors suggest that the AirPods 5 will be unveiled next week alongside the iPhone 18 Pro, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12, as well as the iPhone Ultra. Here's what we know so far about the new AirPods.

The AirPods 5 is expected to debut at the September 9 event in two models, but without a camera.

Apple's biggest annual event will be held next week on September 9. In addition to new iPhones, Apple Watch models, and possibly new home products, the AirPods 5 is also expected to make its first appearance at the event.

The AirPods 4 was launched in 2024, and Apple has typically spaced its AirPods releases two to three years apart. AirPods debuted in 2016, AirPods 2 arrived in 2019, AirPods 3 came in 2021, and AirPods 4 was released in 2024. Based on this cycle, a release this year roughly aligns with past patterns.

However, surprisingly, there haven't been many rumors or leaks about the new AirPods in the market.

Most recent AirPods rumors have centered on a new model equipped with a camera. A video leaked earlier from Apple's software showed what appeared to be the interface for a camera-equipped model, sparking speculation that the product was about to launch.

However, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman says that AirPods with a camera won't arrive until 2027. But he expects the AirPods 5 (without a camera) to make its first appearance at Apple's September event. He recently wrote:

Gurman added in a post on X that the AirPods 5 will come in two different models:

  • With Active Noise Cancellation (ANC)
  • Without Active Noise Cancellation

Gurman previously mentioned in his reporting that he expects the AirPods 5 will not include the heart rate sensor found on the AirPods Pro 3, but that Apple is "looking into adding more health features to AirPods in the future, including a body temperature sensor." He also noted that Apple is "developing the H3 chip, with the goal of reducing latency and improving sound quality."

It remains uncertain whether the AirPods 5 will adopt the H3 chip. When Apple introduced the H2 chip, it was initially exclusive to the AirPods Pro lineup.

However, new health sensors and the H3 chip could potentially make their way into the AirPods 5. Beyond that, details about the AirPods 5 remain fairly limited at this stage. Perhaps, just as with the earlier launch of the AirPods Max 2 this year, Apple may still have a few surprises in store for the AirPods 5 reveal.

What features do you most hope Apple's next-generation AirPods will include? Let us know in the comments.
